solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Gradually worried on account of British infotech

parts.note: a dog that worried something bit at it
by can mean because of, as in 'by reason of'
IT is information technology

explanation.surface: Someone grows slowly anxious about Britain's computer systems.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a little at a time, one small piece after another, so it is a synonym of gradually.

clue.text: Immobile excavator losing motorway time

indicators.note: losing means the motorway letter drops out of the digger word

parts.note: a miner digs out ore, so is an excavator
M is the abbreviation for motorway, as in the M1

explanation.surface: A digger stuck still, having lost time on the motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excavator' suggests a machine, but it is a person: MINER.
explanation.definitionFit: Inert means without power to move or act, so it is a synonym of immobile.

clue.text: Extra husband in family for fellowship

indicators.note: in places the extra and the husband within the family

parts.note: a brood is a family of young
other can mean additional, as in 'other options'

explanation.surface: An additional husband joins the family for companionship.
explanation.definitionFit: A brotherhood is a fraternity or association of companions, a synonym of fellowship.

clue.text: Wolves supporter may do this to travel simply

definitions.meaning: a fan of Wolves, the Wolverhampton Wanderers football club, would back the team; a supporter of wolves would back the pack
to go hiking or touring cheaply with one's kit on one's back

explanation.walkthrough: Wolves is the nickname of Wolverhampton Wanderers, an English football club; a group of wolves is a pack.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it means support a group of wolves; as one word it is cheap travel with a rucksack.

clue.text: Stage work that old Beethoven failed to hear

definitions.meaning: a stage musical by Rodgers and Hammerstein

definitions.text: that old Beethoven failed to hear
definitions.meaning: Beethoven grew deaf in later life and could not hear what he composed

explanation.definitionFit: It names the famous Rodgers and Hammerstein musical and, literally, what a deaf composer could no longer hear.

clue.text: Cut maize, perhaps, and wrap

definitions.meaning: a strip of mown crop lying in a row, maize being one example of a crop
to bind or wrap in cloth

explanation.definitionFit: A noun sense, a band of cut corn, and a verb sense, to bandage or envelop, share one spelling.

clue.text: Shoot a person too easily led

definitions.meaning: a new stem growing from a plant's root or base
a gullible person who is readily duped

explanation.definitionFit: In gardening the word is a side shoot from a root; in slang it is a dupe who is easily fooled.

clue.text: Large growth in koala's habitat

indicators.note: in tells us the letters are found inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A big tree sprouting where a koala lives.
explanation.definitionFit: The ash is a tall tree, and a tree can be called a growth.

clue.text: He and wife no more rent?

definitions.text: He and wife no more rent?

indicators.note: rent means torn apart, so these letters are ripped up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A couple who no longer pay a landlord.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rent' reads as payment to a landlord but is the past tense of rend, torn, signalling the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A couple who own their house no longer pay rent, which describes property owners exactly.

clue.text: Daring arrangement for English choir

indicators.note: a musical arrangement reworks material, so these letters are set out anew

explanation.surface: A bold new musical setting written for an English choir.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrangement' looks musical, fitting the choir, but it signals rearranging E plus CHOIR.
explanation.definitionFit: Heroic and daring both describe bold, brave conduct, so they are synonyms as adjectives.

clue.text: Picture City chief executive not quite in the centre of photo

parts.note: EC is the postcode of the City of London
CE is an abbreviation for chief executive

indicators.note: not quite means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: someone who is in is at home

indicators.note: the centre of a five-letter word is its third letter

explanation.surface: A shot of a City boss placed slightly off-centre in a photograph.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not quite' trims HOME (from 'in', at home) to HOM; 'the centre of' picks the middle O of 'photo'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecce Homo, Latin for 'behold the man', names a painting showing Christ crowned with thorns, so it is a kind of picture.

clue.text: State area in central Monmouthshire

indicators.note: in places the area letter within the picked letters
central asks for the middle letters of the long county name

explanation.surface: A district in the middle of the Welsh county of Monmouthshire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'central' picks UTH, the middle three letters of Monmouthshire, and A goes inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: Utah is one of the fifty states of the USA.

clue.text: For information one has to run for parent

parts.note: pro means in favour of
gen is British slang for information
I is the Roman numeral for one
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Someone needing information must run to find a parent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' is a link: I has TO R after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A progenitor is an ancestor or forebear, someone from whom a line descends, as a parent is.

clue.text: Tons aboard ocean liner at sea consent to only one view

indicators.note: aboard puts the tons letter inside the ship
at sea means confused, so the ship's letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Tonnes of cargo on a liner sailing the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' rearranges OCEAN LINER, and 'aboard' puts T among those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Intolerance is refusing to accept views other than one's own, allowing just a single opinion.

clue.text: Man I care about is from across the Atlantic

indicators.note: about means turned around, so these letters are shuffled into a new order

explanation.surface: A man insists that what he cares about comes from the far side of the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: Seen from Britain, someone from the United States comes from across the Atlantic.

clue.text: Lots keeping fit over marriage

indicators.note: keeping means holding the fitness and over inside

parts.note: many means lots
trim means in good physical shape
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: Plenty of people staying in shape after their wedding.
explanation.definitionFit: Matrimony is the state of being married, a synonym of marriage.

clue.text: Very little can remove point of rising from yeast

parts.note: a tin is a can

indicators.note: remove tells us to take the compass point out of the word yeast

parts.note: the sun rises in the east, a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A tiny amount may stop bread made with yeast from rising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'remove ... from' asks for EAST, the compass point where the sun rises, to come out of YEAST, leaving Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiny means extremely small, a direct synonym of very little.

clue.text: One taking over companies he's floating?

definitions.text: One taking over companies he's floating?

parts.words: One taking over companies he's floating?
parts.note: reads as a tycoon floating firms on the stock market, but means someone carrying groups of people over water

explanation.walkthrough: Taking over and floating suggest business takeovers and share flotations; here they mean carrying passengers across water on a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A boatman who carries people across a river takes companies of passengers over while afloat.

clue.text: Man missing in the wings is Titania's lover

indicators.note: the wings of a word are its two ends, here dropped; also a theatre joke about offstage space

parts.note: in A Midsummer Night's Dream the fairy queen Titania falls for the weaver Bottom

explanation.surface: An actor who should be in the wings is absent, and he plays the fairy queen's lover.
explanation.walkthrough: The theatre wings fit Shakespeare's play, but here they are the outer letters B and M of BOTTOM.
explanation.definitionFit: Otto is a man's first name, and crosswords freely use 'man' to clue a male name.

clue.text: Ruler's operation in wartime

definitions.meaning: Operation ... was the codename for the 1944 Allied invasion of Normandy

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a lord over other lords, a ruler; the other is the codename of the D-Day landings in the Second World War.

clue.text: Bar shortly must introduce a litre

indicators.note: introduce means to insert, here the a and litre go inside

parts.note: soon means shortly, in a little while

explanation.surface: A pub will soon be required to serve drinks by the litre.
explanation.definitionFit: A saloon is a bar, in Britain the more comfortable room of a pub.

clue.text: Flautist, say, improvising jazz in commercial ship

parts.note: a flautist plays a wind instrument, so is an example of the wind section
to jam is to improvise jazz, so one doing it is a jammer

explanation.surface: A flute player busks jazz on board a cargo vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: A flautist improvising jazz would be a 'wind jammer', making this almost a double definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A windjammer is a large merchant sailing vessel, a ship built for trade.

clue.text: Capital equipment beginning to appreciate

parts.note: a rig is a set of equipment, as in a drilling rig

indicators.note: beginning to points at the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Capital equipment starting to grow in value, as an investor might hope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital equipment' reads as a business term, but 'Capital' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Riga is the capital city of Latvia.

clue.text: Paint a little county society

parts.note: Glos is the short form of Gloucestershire, an English county

explanation.surface: Decorating materials for a small rural society.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a little' says the county appears in shortened form: Glos, for Gloucestershire in western England.
explanation.definitionFit: Gloss is a shiny paint, a type of paint.

clue.text: Note number among deer and game

indicators.note: among puts the note and number inside the deer

parts.note: does are female deer
mi is the third note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A musical note and a number turn up among deer and other quarry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'game' sits beside 'deer' as if meaning hunted animals; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Dominoes is a game played with small spotted tiles.

clue.text: Father's dismissed son in anger

indicators.note: dismissed means sent away, so the son letter is removed

parts.note: a sire is a father

explanation.surface: A father sends his son away in a rage.
explanation.definitionFit: Ire is a literary synonym of anger, meaning wrath.

clue.text: Fish pub served up during harvest

indicators.note: during places the pub within the harvest word

parts.note: to mow is to cut down a crop
an inn is a pub, here one put forward by the setter

explanation.surface: Fish is on the pub menu at harvest time.
explanation.definitionFit: A minnow is a small freshwater fish of the carp family.

clue.text: Heraldic beast with very strange name

indicators.note: strange signals the next word's letters are made odd and rearranged

explanation.surface: A coat-of-arms creature with a very odd name.
explanation.definitionFit: A wyvern is a winged two-legged dragon found on coats of arms.

clue.text: Summarise what's new in key Danish city

parts.note: C is a musical key

indicators.note: in places the new letter inside the Danish city

parts.note: Odense is a city in Denmark, birthplace of Hans Christian Andersen

explanation.surface: Someone asks for a quick summary of what is new in a Danish city.
explanation.definitionFit: To condense a text is to shorten it, so it is a synonym of summarise.
